title: Prove sharp high-weight excess 11 at four labels and length ten (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped combinatorial proof answering unpaidmoon’s merged #4148 Open next question 3 at `(n,L)=(4,10)`.

```text
one omitted coordinate => preserving edges form a matching
matching degree identities => only (5,5) and (6,4) class splits
exact F2^3 supports => sharp excess 11 < substituted budget 13
```

Every weight-three functional has exact maximum excess 11 on simple restored length-ten walks on F2^4. Equality means the four-point class is an affine plane. A universal witness attains the cap for every omitted coordinate. The all-ones functional always has excess 6. The matching balance lemma and structural proof are the new result; predecessor measurements are cited premises and are not audited or replayed.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit unpaidmoon #4148 for the open question, double-transversal proof and excess convention; Nick Petalas #3699/#3733, Nicholas Stone #2973, James Reed #3096 and Ross Richardson #943 for the retained classification, correction and prefix-walk lineage. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Evidence

Before: #4148 explicitly leaves a proof of the measured `(4,10)` soundness open. After: a written structural proof, sharp bound/equality criterion and standalone exact corroboration in `research/f7-four-stay-pruning/`.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-four-stay-pruning
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/f7-four-stay-pruning/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/f7-four-stay-pruning/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/f7-four-stay-pruning --check-source-history
```

CPython 3.12, standard library only. Both registered commands pass locally and each took under one second. The timed direct checks took 0.18s and 0.17s; these are local timeout checks, not performance comparisons. Output:

```text
PASS_F7_FOUR_STAY_PRUNING labeled_cycles=2640 functional_checks=13200 max_weight3=11 max_weight4=6 substituted_budget=13 controls=9
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/f7-four-stay-pruning outcome=completed
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES
```

The separate set calculation checks all 8,008 ten-point subsets and five high-weight functionals, retaining 35,280 pairs with the allowed splits, including 3,920 equality cases. Nine mathematical/input controls pass. Fresh SHA256-bound receipts, numeric/Boolean/source receipt mutations, occupied-output preservation, official committed export integrity and optimized Git-free replay pass. All five committed files match tested bytes. Declared source history is available through canonical main `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`.

## Limitations

The theorem concerns simple restored length-ten singleton-prefix walks on F2^4 and functionals of weight at least three. Lower weights can exceed the budget, as the literal control shows. Other dimensions/lengths, partial-prefix pruning, engine integration, seven-label exclusions and the complete multiplication theorem remain outside scope. No new kappa, supplier admission or selected-frontier change. No predecessor executable, large census, Lean or selected cold replay was run.

Overlap coverage included 411 open PRs and 3,925 Discussion records, live relevant PR bodies/claims, recent account submissions, distinctive all-main README searches and merged-term searches. The cached local scan omitted 6,186 of 6,319 tracked notes; relevant f7 READMEs were read directly from Git. Arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain limits.

## Related open work

- #4871 binds length-22 seven-label receipts to the derived split domain; this proof concerns the distinct four-label length-ten high-weight excess boundary and does not replay those receipts.
- #3899 audits a partial union-support prune at `(4,8)` with revisits; this result proves a sharp complete-cycle excess theorem at `(4,10)` under simplicity. No shared numerical audit is claimed.

Refresh after hosted CI: none of the nine other open contributions from this account created since the advance CLAIM studies this word/excess quantity. No additional related entry or shared-number comparison is required.

## Open next questions

- Prove the `(5,12)` high-weight case from #4148, beginning with matching balance and the remaining `(8,4)` split in a four-dimensional kernel.
- Derive a sound partial-prefix completion bound from the matching constraint before considering engine integration.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed at head `2e95d12a8f1557a90102314a773c74420bcbd4fe` in [Registered research packages run 39870228095](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39870228095): `plan` in 2m31s and the registered package `replay` in 1m11s. Run metadata confirms this exact head, completed status and success. The replay executes the warning-strict normal and optimized commands. Local metadata/pins, committed-byte/source-history preflight, export integrity, receipt controls and Git-free replay also passed. These checks corroborate the scoped proof and do not certify the complete multiplication theorem.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated. Only one new five-file research package is added; existing engines and selected-frontier files are untouched.
